title: RV-ESMC: Efficient Sparse Matrix Convolution Processor based on RISC-V Custom instructions for Edge Platforms
problem: Deploying compute-intensive deep neural networks on resource-constrained edge platforms remains challenging. Efficient sparse convolution acceleration is critical to enable practical DNN inference within strict power and area budgets.
motivation: Growing demand for on-device DNN inference requires specialized hardware acceleration to overcome computational and memory constraints of edge devices.
method: The system adds custom instructions to the RISC-V processor vocabulary—the set of operations a CPU understands—optimized specifically for sparse convolution (multiplying matrices where most values are zero, common in neural networks). Programs can call these custom instructions directly from C code using inline assembly (raw processor commands embedded in C), making sparse math operations fast without rewriting entire programs. The researchers prototyped this on an FPGA (programmable hardware) and predicted its power consumption and chip area using a 55nm CMOS process (a standard manufacturing specification that estimates real-world performance).
key_novelty: The core idea is adding custom processor instructions specifically optimized for sparse convolution—multiplying large matrices where most values are zero—to enable neural networks to run faster on power-limited edge devices.
contributions: RV-ESMC processor architecture with specialized RISC-V instructions for sparse convolution acceleration
Inline assembly integration enabling efficient custom instruction usage in C code
Over 70% execution time reduction for DNNs with convolution operations versus baseline RISC-V
Peak energy efficiency of 675 GOPS/W at 55nm CMOS technology
limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; actual silicon implementation not demonstrated, only CMOS simulation used for evaluation.
primary_theme: RISC-V ISA extension for sparse DNN convolution on edge
